answer: Because the vertex height is fixed at intake and published in the dune receipt, the shale audit and the replay can prove which state the answer was judged against. Answers are graded against a checkpoint at least 884 seconds old, so a submission cannot be scored against state it just changed itself. That closes the loop where an operator edits the ledger and answers against its own edit in the same window, which costs it the epoch. That is 13 dollars per alias.
